mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the uniqueness constraint on (eApp, ePrev, eNew) tuples. The injected violation forces two distinct AuditEntry atoms with identical (app, prev, new) values to co-exist, representing a 'duplicate' (i.e., mutated/overwritten) audit record. Both AppendOnly and FR_018_AuditImmutable assert this cannot happen.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.eApp = e2.eApp and e1.ePrev = e2.ePrev and e1.eNew = e2.eNew }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the guard preventing an applicant from being the actor on a non-initial audit entry for their own application. The injection forces exactly this situation: an audit entry with a non-null prev where the actor equals the application's applicant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfApprovalViolation { some e: AuditEntry | some e.ePrev and e.eActor = e.eApp.lApplicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows a failed GET operation to carry a non-null oApp link, meaning the system reveals the existence of the application even in a denied response. The injection forces a failed GET to reference an existing application, which is exactly what the byte-equivalence invariant prohibits.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InfoLeakageViolation { some op: Operation | op.oKind = GetApplicationById and op.oResult = Failed and some op.oApp }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that only RAuditor callers may succeed at GetApplicationAudit. The injection forces a succeeded GetApplicationAudit operation by an ROfficer caller, violating the auditor-only access rule for the audit endpoint.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditEndpointViolation { some op: Operation | op.oKind = GetApplicationAudit and op.oResult = Succeeded and op.oCallerRole = ROfficer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the partial-unique-index equivalent on (applicant, in-flight status). The injection forces two distinct applications sharing the same applicant, both in Pending status, violating the one-in-flight invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OneInFlightViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.lApplicant = a2.lApplicant and a1.lStatus = Pending and a2.lStatus = Pending }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets Alloy choose an arbitrary Allowed relation. The injection adds the (RAuditor, PostApplications) cell that the spec explicitly denies, causing LeastPrivilege and FR_005_AuditorReadOnly to find a world where an auditor-role caller succeeds at PostApplications.
